broken_sector_GNS_gap.definition: For a selected algebraic ground state omega, define the state-vector Poincare gap Delta_omega^P=inf sigma(H_omega restricted to Omega_omega perpendicular). A positive value implies ker(H_omega)=C Omega_omega and then equals inf(sigma(H_omega) minus {0}); without a simple kernel it is zero.
broken_sector_GNS_gap.poincare: Delta_omega^P is equivalently the best constant on a generator core in <A Omega,H_omega A Omega>>=Delta_omega^P[omega(A^*A)-|omega(A)|^2]
broken_sector_GNS_gap.block_falsifier: For S_B=sum_(y in B)Q_y, [S_B,[H,S_B]]=hbar^2|B|/chi and Delta_omega^P<=hbar^2|B|/[2chi Var_omega(S_B)]
broken_sector_GNS_gap.necessary_condition: A positive state-vector Poincare gap requires Var_omega(S_B)=O(|B|); if Var_omega(S_B)/|B| diverges along blocks then Delta_omega^P=0. A positive spectral gap above a separately degenerate zero eigenspace instead requires projection off the full kernel and is not decided by ordinary variance.
broken_sector_GNS_gap.ordered_tangent: At the collective classical ordered point x^2=-r/g the Q3 Walsh Hessian levels are -2r+lambda(-r/g)ell+2cE(k), ell=0,2,4,6, so the tree-level minimum -2r is positive; this is viability evidence only
broken_sector_GNS_gap.boundary: The O(1/V) full finite-volume gap collapse is the symmetry-tunnelling channel and determines neither the connected block variance nor the pure-sector GNS gap. Linear variance control is necessary but not sufficient for the full Poincare inequality, and simplicity of the selected GNS ground vector has not been proved.
